sources.entry: google-adk - Google's code-first toolkit for building, evaluating, and deploying AI agents.

summary.one_liner: Google's open-source, code-first Python framework for building, evaluating, and deploying AI agents, optimized for Gemini but model-agnostic.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes ADK as a modular framework for defining agents, tools, and orchestration directly in Python. It provides a graph-based Workflow runtime with routing, fan-out/fan-in, loops, retry, state management, dynamic nodes, human-in-the-loop, and nested workflows. A Task API covers agent-to-agent delegation, and agents can be composed into multi-agent hierarchies. Tools can be custom functions, OpenAPI specs, MCP tools, or pre-built tools, and a tool confirmation flow can gate execution. The CLI offers `adk run` for interactive use, `adk web` for a development UI, `adk eval` for evaluation, and `adk deploy` for Docker or Google Cloud Run.
use_cases: build a multi-agent AI application in Python
orchestrate agent workflows with branching and loops
add human approval before an agent runs a tool
evaluate agent behavior against test sets
deploy an agent to Cloud Run or Docker
connect agents to MCP or OpenAPI tools
notable: Graph-based Workflow runtime with fan-out/fan-in, loops, retry, and human-in-the-loop
Built-in development UI for testing, evaluating, and debugging agents
Sibling ADK implementations in Java, Kotlin, Go, and TypeScript
Agent Config feature for building agents without code
Community repo for third-party integrations and deployment scripts
caveats: Development version from main may contain experimental changes or bugs
